summary_en: Suruga Bank raised its dividend forecast for fiscal year ending March 2027 by 20 yen per share to 80 yen, comprising 40 yen interim and 40 yen year-end dividends, following upward revision of full-year earnings guidance driven by strong loan origination and higher interest rates.
title_en: Notice Regarding Revision of Business Forecast and Revision of Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
Suruga Bank announced on September 30, 2026 that it would raise its dividend forecast for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027. The interim dividend per share has been increased by 10 yen to 40 yen, and the year-end dividend has likewise been increased by 10 yen to 40 yen, resulting in a total annual dividend increase of 20 yen to 80 yen per share.

The dividend hike follows an upward revision of the company's earnings guidance. Recurring profit for the full year is now projected at 56.0 billion yen, up 8.5 billion yen from the previous forecast, with net income attributable to parent company shareholders revised upward by 12.0 billion yen to 44.0 billion yen. Per-share earnings are forecast at 262.01 yen, compared to the prior projection of 187.72 yen.

The company cited strong performance in its core loan business, with new loan originations and the incorporation of higher interest rates tracking ahead of plan. Additionally, the revaluation methodology for real estate collateral on multi-unit rental property loans, implemented in the first quarter, generated reversals of loan loss provisions exceeding expectations. The company stated that the dividend increase reflects its shareholder return policy applied in light of the upgraded earnings outlook, capital soundness, and future financial position.
